The last time we meet as we always have, for no reason beyond wanting to see each other's faces.

I want this precious time, at least, to end with us smiling together.

“Sakura, are you awake? It's late, but let's have lunch.”

I knock and enter the room.

Sakura seems to have been asleep, but her face lights up the moment I enter.

“—Yes. I'm glad you came, Shirou.”

She smiles gently, looking truly happy.

桜はくすり、と安心したように笑い、
「じゃあお花見とかしたいです、わたし」
そんな、ささやかな願いを口にした。
pages.en:
“Anywhere. Once people set their minds to it, there's nowhere they can't go.”

I mean it sincerely, but Sakura seems to take it as a joke.

She gives a soft, relieved laugh.

“Then I'd like to go see the cherry blossoms.”

She gives voice to that modest wish.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yeah. There’s nowhere you can’t go if you put your mind to it.”
I’m serious, but it seems she took it as a joke.
Sakura smiles with relief.
“Then I want to go cherry blossom viewing.”
And she makes a trivial wish.

pages.ja:
「花見？ 花見って、あの花見か？」
「はい。このお屋敷でも出来ますけど、あるのは梅の木だけですから。天気のいい日に、広い野原で先輩とお花見がしたいです」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“The cherry blossoms? You mean flower viewing?”

“Yes. We could do it here at the house, but there are only plum trees in the garden. On a fine day, I'd like to sit with you in a wide-open field and look at the cherry blossoms.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Cherry blossom viewing? You mean that cherry blossom viewing?”
“Yes. We can do it here, but there are only plum trees here. I want to go cherry blossom viewing in a big field on a sunny day.”

pages.ja:
「
そっか。それは、確かに」
すごく楽しそうだ。
橋の下の公園で、雲一つない青空を見上げながら、春の樹を見るのもいい。
楽しいコトなんて山ほどある筈だ。
その門出が花見だっていうのは、桜に凄く似合っている。

pages.en:
“—I see. That really does…”

It sounds wonderful.

We could sit in the park beneath the bridge, looking up at the trees of spring beneath a cloudless blue sky.

There must be countless things that can bring us joy.

And for Sakura to take the first step into that new life beneath the cherry blossoms feels entirely fitting.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
I see. That certainly…”
…Sounds really fun.
It’ll be great to watch cherry blossoms under a clear blue sky at the park by the bridge.
There are many fun things.
Starting out with cherry blossom viewing suits Sakura.

pages.ja:
「
よし。じゃあ約束だ。桜の体が治って、このゴタゴタが終わったら二人で行こう」
桜は満足そうに微笑む。
そんな約束をして、ゆっくりと立ち上がった。
pages.jaRuby:
「
よし。じゃあ約束だ。桜の体が治って、このゴタゴタが終わったら二人で行こう」
桜は満足そうに微笑む。
そんな約束をして、ゆっくりと立ち上がった。
pages.en:
“—Good. Then it's a promise. Once you're better and this whole mess is over, we'll go together.”

Sakura smiles contentedly.

With that promise made, I slowly rise.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
All right. Then it’s a promise. Let’s go there together once you get well and once this whole mess is over.”
Sakura shows a satisfied smile.
I make the promise and stand up.

pages.ja:
……そう。
本当に、そうできたらどんなに幸福だろう、と。
十年前の火事から一度も思わなかった、自らの幸福を夢に見た。
pages.jaRuby:
……そう。

pages.en:
…Yes.

How happy I would be if we could truly do that.

For the first time since the fire ten years ago, I dream of happiness for myself.
pages.mirrorMoon:
……Yes.
How great will it be if we can really do that?
I imagine my own happiness that I’ve never imagined since the fire ten years ago.

pages.ja:
客間を去る。
残ったものは些細な約束だけ。
それは桜だけの望みじゃない。
その、四月にさえなれば幾らでも叶えられる願いは、俺自身の願いでもある。

I leave the guest room.

Only a small promise remains behind.

It is not Sakura's wish alone.

That wish, so easily fulfilled if only we reach April, belongs to me as well.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I leave her room.
All that’s left is a trivial promise.
It’s not just Sakura’s wish.
This promise, which can be fulfilled come April, is my wish as well.
